entries.title: Bond-percolation connectivity operator on counting measure
entries.statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on a countable graph G=(V,E), each edge is independently open with probability p. Write tau_p(x,y)=P_p(x and y are connected by a finite open path), allowing a path of length zero. The connectivity kernel T_p has entries tau_p(x,y) and acts initially on finitely supported functions by (T_p f)(x)=sum_y tau_p(x,y)f(y). Boundedness means that this action extends to a bounded operator on l2(V) with counting measure.

entries.title: Draft conditional route from a critical connectivity norm
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent review pending. On a countable simple graph of maximum degree D, if p<1 and the counting-measure connectivity operator T_p has norm M<infinity, then independent sprinkling with epsilon D M<1 gives ||T_(p+(1-p)epsilon)|| <= M/(1-epsilon D M). On an infinite connected quasi-transitive graph with pc<1, a finite norm M=||T_pc|| would therefore yield pu>=pc+(1-pc)/(2DM)>pc. The missing input is a finite critical norm for every prescribed nonamenable Cayley graph; nonamenability has not been shown here to supply it. This is a sufficient route, not a solution of the universal conjecture.

entries.title: Draft route through separated pairs above criticality
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent review pending. For Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph, one parameter p1>pc with inf_(x,y) tau_p1(x,y)=0 would imply pu>=p1>pc. Entrywise monotonicity propagates the zero infimum to every q<=p1, whereas almost-sure uniqueness and FKG give a strictly positive uniform lower bound on tau_q. Thus uniform exponential connectivity decay at a strictly supercritical parameter is sufficient for nonuniqueness, without proving an l2 norm bound. The unresolved input is to produce separated pairs above pc for every prescribed nonamenable Cayley graph.
assumptions: Infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph
Zero infimum of connectivity at p1

entries.title: Draft obstruction to inferring an operator bound from exponential decay
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent review pending. On the 4-regular tree, a Cayley graph of the free group on two generators, Bernoulli bond connectivity is tau_p(o,x)=p^dist(o,x). It decays exponentially for every p<1, but the squared row sum is 1+4p^2 sum_(j>=0)(3p^2)^j and diverges whenever p>=1/sqrt(3). Hence the counting-measure l2 operator is unbounded there. At p=3/4 the radius-R partial sum is exactly 1+(36/11)((27/16)^R-1). This refutes the decay-to-l2 inference; it does not refute the nonuniqueness conjecture or critical operator boundedness. The zero-infimum criterion still holds at this parameter.

entries.title: Draft correction to spectral-criterion normalization
entries.statement: DRAFT source correction, independent review pending. If rho is the simple-random-walk spectral radius on a d-regular Cayley graph and A is its adjacency operator, then ||A||=d rho. The Benjamini-Schramm sufficient spectral criterion is p d rho<1 at a percolating parameter p; in particular pc d rho<1 suffices for pc<pu. Omitting d and using pc<1/rho misstates that argument: nonamenability gives rho<1, so the omitted-factor inequality is automatic since pc<=1. For the 4-regular tree, pc=1/3 and rho=sqrt(3)/2, so pc d rho=2sqrt(3)/3>1; the sufficient spectral argument does not cover this graph even though its nonuniqueness phase is known.
assumptions: The spectral criterion is sufficient, not equivalent to the conjecture

relations.rationale: The conditional sprinkling route assumes a finite norm of exactly the counting-measure connectivity operator defined here.
The sufficient zero-infimum criterion is expressed in the entries tau_p of this operator; no l2 boundedness is assumed.
At p=3/4 on the 4-regular tree, the connectivity infimum is zero while the l2 row sum diverges, so the separated-pairs input is weaker than a finite operator norm at that parameter.
The adjacency resolvent supplies a sufficient norm regime only when p||A||=p d rho<1. Nonamenability alone does not establish this regime at pc.

The existing attempt says 'p_c < 1/rho where rho is the spectral radius of simple random walk'. The primary Theorem 4 instead displays 'rho(G)kp < 1'. This link identifies the exact stored attribution requiring the degree-factor correction; it does not endorse the attempt or resolve its parent conjecture.
